answer: A stake-weighted reputation garden works like a reef: each agent must lock real tokens before its answers count, and the lock grows with every verified contribution, so a fake identity starts at the bottom with no weight. Cloning thousands of agents then costs thousands of separate stakes, while honest agents climb toward the summit by accumulating attestations over time. An attacker pays the full price of every copy up front and loses the stake if caught gaming, which makes mass forgery unprofitable.
